# dat_renamer

[← Command index](README.md)

Rename ROM files to the names a DAT file gives them, matching by MD5.

## Synopsis

```
dat_renamer [options]
```

## Description

Loads ROM records from either every clrmamepro XML `.dat` file under `-d` (searched
recursively), or a cache file given with `-c`; `-d` wins when both are given. Records
without a name, size, CRC and MD5 are ignored.

Then every file under `-i`, recursively, is hashed with MD5. A file whose hash matches
a record is renamed, in its own directory, to the ROM file name from that record.
Files with no match are left alone.

With `-d` and `-g`, the collected records are also written to the `-c` path so later
runs can load them with `-c` alone. The cache holds one ROM per line as
`game || file || size || crc || md5`.

## Options

### General

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-i, --input_path <input_path>` | Directory of files to rename, searched recursively. Required. |
| `-d, --dat_directory <dat_directory>` | Directory of clrmamepro XML `.dat` files to read ROM records from. |
| `-c, --dat_cachefile <dat_cachefile>` | Cache file to read ROM records from, or with `-g` to write them to. |
| `-g, --generate_cachefile` | With `-d`, write the collected records to the `-c` cache file. |

### Common options

| Option | Description |
|--------|-------------|
| `-v, --verbose` | Enable verbose mode. |
| `-p, --pretend_run` | Do a pretend run with no permanent changes. |
| `-x, --exit_on_failure` | Enable exit on failure mode. |
| `--no-preview` | Skip the preview confirmation prompt. |

## Examples

### Rename using a folder of DAT files

```bash
dat_renamer -i ~/Roms/Unsorted -d ~/Dats
```

### Rename and save a cache of the DAT records

```bash
dat_renamer -i ~/Roms/Unsorted -d ~/Dats -g -c ~/Dats/cache.txt
```

### Rename using a saved cache

```bash
dat_renamer -i ~/Roms/Unsorted -c ~/Dats/cache.txt
```

### Dry run

```bash
dat_renamer -i ~/Roms/Unsorted -d ~/Dats -p -v
```

## Notes

- When two DAT records share an MD5, the one read last is used.
- A renamed file replaces any file already at the new name.
